"Job gains were solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate declined." This, combined with the Committee’s view that Q1 weakness was “transitory,” points to a modestly positive tone. From a policy-rule perspective, the hold-then-gradualism stance is consistent with estimated forward-looking Taylor-type rules (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), which tends to anchor expectations and support risk sentiment. The explicit emphasis on a symmetric 2 percent inflation goal and data dependence aligns with inflation-forecast targeting principles (Svensson and Woodford, 2005), reducing the risk of premature tightening. Continued reinvestment of MBS and Treasuries keeps term premiums and external finance premia contained, consistent with financial accelerator insights (Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist), which is supportive for growth-sensitive assets. Operationally, control of the funds rate via IOER and ON RRP underscores credible implementation (Goodfriend, 2002). Offsetting this, “low” market-based inflation compensation tempers optimism. Netting these, the sentiment is slightly more positive than neutral.
